text: Require contextual review before MCP aim creation
description: Make MCP aim creation an enforced two-call review. First create_aim call performs text+semantic search across active and cancelled aims, returns compact relevant context plus a deterministic confirmation token, and writes nothing. A second identical call with that token creates the aim. Similarity is informative rather than an automatic veto: the agent may confirm a genuinely distinct aim. The token binds the exact proposal so edits require fresh context. Keep this separate and much leaner than the human-facing transient subtree approval system.

status.comment: Two-step contextual creation gate is implemented and internally verified; awaiting Felix's acceptance. The running MCP client must be restarted later to expose the new schema/behavior.

reflection: Implemented an enforced MCP-only two-call creation gate. First create_aim call performs existing combined text+semantic search, returns up to eight related active/cancelled aims with status rationale and a deterministic token, and writes nothing. Second identical call with the token creates; changing any proposal field invalidates it. Similarity remains contextual rather than an automatic veto. This is intentionally separate from the richer human-facing subtree proposal system. Verification: focused MCP aims+phases tests 16/16 pass, including no-write preview, cancelled rationale visibility, mismatch rejection, and confirmed creation; MCP TypeScript build passes.
